topics.label: Lecture framing: cancer evolution and the microenvironment
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the audience, places the lecture within the series, and states the themes and learning aims for the lecture.

topics.label: Mutation accumulation and clonal selection in cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how mutations can give clones a growth advantage and how selection among clones contributes to tumor progression.

topics.label: Epigenetic disruption in tumor development
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic shows that transient changes to chromatin and gene transcription can contribute to tumor development even without new mutations.

topics.label: Stemness and cell of origin in tumor growth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine whether cancer growth follows a stem-cell-like hierarchy and how the cell type in which mutations occur can influence tumor development.

topics.label: Inflammation-induced stemness in cancer initiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how inflammatory signals can provide conditions that let mutated cells acquire stem-like properties and form tumors.

topics.label: Microenvironmental support of established tumors and therapeutic targeting
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains that established tumors can depend on surrounding cells and signals, and considers targeting that support as a therapeutic strategy.

topics.label: Methods for studying cancer evolution and cell interactions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes sequencing, computational analysis, and spatial profiling as ways to investigate tumor-cell states and their interactions.

topics.label: An integrated evolutionary view of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes the lecture's argument that mutations, cell properties, and environmental conditions can combine to enable malignant growth.

topics.label: Lecture close and next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic ends the lecture and announces the subject of the next meeting.
